OneDrive is an absolute cancer... students constantly accidentally checking their repos out onto onedrive which makes performance atrocious. The UI in Windows is intentionally designed to confuse the issue so people unintentionally end up using OneDrive, which is free until it isn't and then they jam you with a subscription.
Helping my mom recover from OneDrive's 'cleanup' was the closest I've come to negotiating with terrorists.
What I hate about it is that it's turned on automatically. It's basically just holding your computer for ransom because the 20 gigabyte they give you for free doesn't cut it.
First thing I do on any Windows machine is uninstall OneDrive anywhere possible. It's caused me enough grief that I just avoid it entirely at this point.
I have had to turn off One Drive after a series of incidents where it deleted or rendered files unrecoverable. It's basically malware to me.
I use OneDrive at work for all of my documents and have never encountered the horror stories I frequently read... I will say that the Microsoft Office OneDrive save experience is completely subpar.

I love OneDrive... they are backed up to the cloud and synced with the other computers I use. Some computers are shared by six family members, each with their own MS account and 1TB of storage... I've never had any problems.

When Word defaulted to OneDrive... I could not save. Needless to say that was the last time I used OneDrive... even if you don't have the OneDrive service running on your PC, Office will store files in OneDrive directly through the API.
Whatever you do, don't try to sync a git repo folder with OneDrive... OneDrive works best if you give it one file.
I found out my mom was paying for OneDrive because her Android phone autosynced a bunch of her files and she ran out of 'space'. She had no idea what it was but the OS pushed it hard.
Fix it by de-selecting 'backup' multiple times and then clicking 'submit'. Files magically re-appear after I make sure to tell Microsoft to 'keep my local copy'.
OD didn't back up your data, it moved it to the cloud and didn't tell you... Disabling the 'backup' means disabling the storage of your single copy of the data.
All I know is that a bunch of files reverted to very old versions and I found no way to recover from that. It was pure loss... OneDrive proved itself untrustworthy.
if a user does not actively change the save location, at least for office apps, the default behavior is to save to onedrive.

The problem isn't that cloud sync/backup is useful. It's that Microsoft isn't respecting users' agency to adopt it or not... turning on OneDrive by default for users who already explicitly chose not to use it.

Microsoft OneDrive for Business modifies files as it syncs... I was using OneDrive (the consumer one) with an Office 365 Home sub for doing basic personal finance spreadsheets and it decided to literally destroy the contents as it was uploaded and downloaded from one computer to another. I can't really trust it.
It's not that OneDrive is modifying files 'as it syncs'; it involves Sharepoint, which adds certain metadata to documents that it handles.
Dropbox, Google Drive and Microsoft OneDrive blocked in Turkey following leaks... this makes doing your work suddenly a lot harder.
